angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,092,945 km at 13.49 pc = 1.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7513: distance 13.492 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.003), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 13.492 +/- 0.04 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 74.1940 +/- 0.2083 mas (same row, RUWE 7.25), 356.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.571 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7513: radius 1.571 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 3.345 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.04) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,092,945 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 6232 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7513: effective temperature 6232 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.027) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 7513: effective temperature 6232 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.027) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
